[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um this is Maya on the Redwood side. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Lena: good, thanks. busy quarter. we'll try to keep this tight.
[00:10] Rajiv: morning all. we want to lock the uplift and get eu nodes before the holiday push.
[00:18] Ethan: quick agenda — headroom, EU staging, security, bench plan, next steps. is that right?
[00:23] Hannah: yep that's right. we ran into some tail latency spikes last week on long prompts so curious about dedicated vs private.
[00:31] Maya: ok great. first up, current usage – can you remind us of the monthly tokens and 95th p99 targets?
[00:38] Lena: sure, we're at about 1.2B tokens / month; p95 around 320ms for short prompts, but p99 for longer sequences jumps to 1.1s. that's with our batching right now.
[00:50] Ethan: got it. based on that profile we recommended a modest dedicated pool plus an EU burst node so you get locality and predictable throughput. private (VPC) adds a bit more ops overhead but keeps data residency — and avoids outbound egress to hosted.
[01:06] Sara: about the private option, we need to confirm KMS integration — can Redwood integrate with our Azure Key Vault or we need to use Redwood KMS/HSM? last time the doc said HSM optional.
[01:18] Ethan: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration; for Azure Key Vault there is a small configuration step, and we can run a handoff with your security team. HSM-backed keys via Redwood Private are also possible if you want on-prem key material. sometimes the transcript generator says H-M-S, sorry.
[01:34] Lena: and SOC2 evidence — we need audit logs with token-level tracing for two teams, and exportable logs for our compliance team.
[01:42] Sofia: we can share our SOC2 pack and the audit log schema; logs can be exported to your SIEM over S3 or direct syslog depending on the plan.
[01:51] Owen: pricing question — what's the unit delta for EU nodes vs US over dedicated? also curious about burst blocks pricing model.
[01:58] Maya: good question. short answer: EU on Dedicated is about 8-12% higher than US-west due to capacity and licensing; burst blocks have a separate commit with no long-term lock, billed monthly when used. we'll put exact numbers in the quote.
[02:10] Rajiv: can we do a 12 month amendment to the retainer with an option to add more burst credit mid-term? we'd like flexibility.
[02:18] Maya: yes, we commonly do a base retainer + optional burst addendum; we'll draft language.
[02:23] Hannah: operationally — if we go VPC private, what's the provisioning timeline? we have a hard go-live target 11/15.
[02:30] Ethan: for VPC private on EU it's about 3 weeks from signed amendment if the peering and IP allowlists are ready; shorter if we do a Dedicated plus VPC peering model. staging can be faster — we can stand up a staging VPC in ~1 week for bench tests.
[02:45] Lena: bench tests — we want to validate p50/p95/p99 across our real prompt sets, KV cache behavior, and also quantized model latency. can Redwood run those or we run them?
[02:55] Ethan: we can run a joint benchmark — Redwood SE will run baseline and then you run end-to-end within the staging VPC. we'll provide test harness scripts and guidance.
[03:06] Maya: actioning that — Ethan will own the benchmark plan.
[03:10] Owen: procurement — what docs do we need for PO? standard SOW + amendment? any special SOC attachments?
[03:16] Maya: SOW + amendment to add EU nodes and burst. we'll include SOC2 attestation and the security appendix. anything procurement-specific we should include?
[03:24] Owen: need the SLA appendix and invoice cadence. also need a list of IP ranges for allowlisting.
[03:30] Sara: security follow-up — are audit logs tokenized? we cannot store raw PII in the logs.
[03:36] Ethan: logs have redaction options; we can redact or hash sensitive fields before export. we'll share the log retention and redaction options in the security packet.
[03:46] Lena: question on model variants — we'd like a lower-cost quantized variant for non-PHI content and the full float model for PHI processing. can routing do that automatically?
[03:55] Ethan: yes — routing policies can be per-route. you can pin certain routes to float models in the private cluster and others to quantized hosted variants. we'll demo the routing rules in the console. sometimes the console name came through in notes as "RedWood console" — spelled weird in transcripts.
[04:12] Rajiv: also failover — if EU capacity saturated, we need automatic fallback to US for non-PII, but block PII movement. is that doable?
[04:20] Ethan: yes, policy-based routing supports that. you can mark a route as "no-failover" for PHI, and for other traffic fallback is allowed. we'll walk through policy examples in the follow-up.
[04:31] Hannah: latency vs cost trade — if we enable more aggressive batching we save cost but p99 increases; want suggestions on tunables.
[04:40] Ethan: we'll provide suggested batching profiles per workload and expected delta on cost/latency. also recommend prefix/KV cache for common sequences — big win for Moraine's dialog workloads.
[04:52] Lena: great. timeline check — we want staging bench week of 10/26, contract signed by 10/27, production EU go-live 11/15. is that realistic?
[05:01] Maya: yes, staging week of 10/26 works; contract by 10/27 is tight but doable if procurement moves quickly; production 11/15 is a stretch but feasible if peering and allowlist are provided immediately.
[05:12] Owen: procurement will try to accelerate; I'll get the PO path and confirm today's discussion to our legal.
[05:18] Sara: I'll review the KMS doc and get back with any open questions.
[05:22] Sofia: i'll open the staging provisioning ticket today and tag Hannah and Rajiv.
[05:26] Maya: excellent. recap — we'll send quote and amendment, security pack, benchmark plan. schedule bench window for 10/26. next call to review bench results after tests.

[05:39] Lena: thanks.
